survey_protocol.gate: walkable = interactive mode + plausible coordinates + right-press dx > 6 px; level = walkable and a nonzero timer

progression_protocol.clear_definition: the engine reached the world map (0x0E) without passing through the death mode (0x0B) on the way; whether the cursor also moved to another node is reported separately, because a clear that leaves the cursor where it was is still a clear

recorder_protocol.conclusion_definition: the engine returned the player to the map (0x0E) without taking a life. The mode byte alone cannot say it: the house session's left-edge exit marches through 0x0B - the byte the death animation owns - on its way out the door, and the byte would call that a death. The lives counter ($7E:0DBE) settles it: an exit leaves it put, a death decrements it, and reaching the map while losing a life is the game-over sequence, not a conclusion
recorder_protocol.outro: every episode keeps recording past the verdict with the controls released, so the video shows the mode march and the map settling instead of freezing on the flipped byte; the telemetry panels freeze on the last gameplay frame because a warp has no residue
recorder_protocol.unplayable_sessions: 0x27 and 0x29: 10.68 measured their floors to stop holding (a measured decor row over air) and 0x29's own scripted pipe ride to lift the player and drop him past the level with the controls untouched - fresh entry or restored savestate alike - so no agent concludes them, and the episodes document what the engine does
recorder_protocol.frontier_rule: RIGHT+Y with the B pulse, stopped at 90 frames of no advance, a spent hold, death, or the frame budget
